_doc: Machine-readable exam format (structure only, no exam content). Counts/times checked against the official pages in verified.sources on verified.date; criteria descriptions are LexKite's own wording. Read by scripts/content-qa/exam-format-check.mjs (docs/CONTENT-QA.md §6).
name: IELTS General Training
total_minutes_note: L 30 + R 60 + W 60 + S 11–14, plus Listening transfer/review time

sections.name: Listening
sections.minutes_note: about 30 min of recording; paper test adds 10 min transfer, computer test 2 min review

parts.name: Part 3
parts.context: educational/training conversation, up to four speakers

rules: answers come in the same order as the recording
word limit stated per task (e.g. ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER)

sections.name: Reading (General Training)

parts.name: Section 1 – social survival
parts.texts: 2–3 short factual texts or several shorter texts (notices, adverts, timetables)

parts.name: Section 3 – general reading
parts.texts: 1 longer, more complex text on a general topic

question_types: mcq (4 options or more answers from a longer list)

sections.name: Writing

tasks.name: Task 1 – letter
types: letter (personal, semi-formal or formal; three bullet points)

rules: connected text, no notes or bullet points
off-topic or copied text is penalised

criteria.name: Task Achievement (Task 1) / Task Response (Task 2)
criteria.focus: Does the answer do everything the prompt asks, with relevant, well-developed and accurate content at the required length?

criteria.name: Coherence and Cohesion
criteria.focus: Is the text logically ordered in paragraphs, with clear progression and linking that helps rather than gets in the way?

criteria.name: Lexical Resource
criteria.focus: How wide, precise and natural is the vocabulary, including collocation and spelling?

criteria.name: Grammatical Range and Accuracy
criteria.focus: How varied are the sentence structures and how many sentences are error-free?

parts.name: Long turn
parts.note: task card with prompts; 1 min preparation; speak up to 2 min; then 1–2 rounding-off questions

parts.name: Discussion
parts.note: more abstract questions linked to the Part 2 topic

criteria.name: Fluency and Coherence
criteria.focus: Can the candidate keep talking at length without unnatural pauses and link ideas clearly?

criteria.name: Lexical Resource
criteria.focus: Range and flexibility of vocabulary, ability to paraphrase when a word is missing.

criteria.name: Grammatical Range and Accuracy
criteria.focus: Mix of simple and complex structures and how often they are accurate.

criteria.name: Pronunciation
criteria.focus: How easy the speech is to understand: sounds, word and sentence stress, rhythm, intonation.

scoring.overall: mean of the four skill bands, rounded to the nearest half band (.25 rounds up to .5, .75 rounds up to the next whole band)
scoring.listening_reading: raw score out of 40 converted to a band by an official conversion table (not reproduced)
scoring.writing: Task 2 counts twice as much as Task 1
